hypothese.summary: Profitable growth thesis post-JS Global spin-off: international acceleration and product innovation support a structural margin expansion, with a first return of capital (750M$ buyback) that reverses the deleveraging.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Post-spin profitable-growth story: since separating from JS Global (July 2023), 12 consecutive quarters of double-digit organic growth on a product-innovation engine (Ninja Luxe Cafe, Ninja Crispi, Shark PowerDetect) and accelerating international expansion (+31.6% in Q1 26), with the Europe/Mexico shift from distributor to direct sales completing by end-Q2 26. The bet: innovation cadence sustains growth while direct-sales mix and supply-chain diversification (out of China) defend margin through the tariff era.

== THESIS READ ==
- The innovation cadence is the moat - each new category (coffee, outdoor, beauty) extends the S-curve. Watch: new-category revenue disclosures.
- Direct-sales transition lifts gross margin but adds opex first - the 2026 print will be mix-noisy. Watch: international margin once the transition completes.
- Tariff exposure is managed via supply-chain shift - execution risk, not thesis risk. Watch: gross-margin bridge quarter by quarter.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Young fiche (created 15/07/2026): dernierCall and guidanceHistory ABSENT by construction - to initialize at the next quarterly report; priorEPS null. 'data' retreated for two true separation one-offs (2022: 34M discretionary bonus; 2023: 82.3M separation costs + 19.5M withholding tax), published figures kept in-fiche for audit traceability. Consensus basis wedge documented (adjusted street vs retreated GAAP).

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: revenue 7,167M (+12%), EBIT 1,061M (14.8%), EPS 5.51; 2027-2030: revenue +8%/yr fading, margin ~15-15.8%, ETR 22% (company's own normalized rate), shares -1%/yr, net debt low and stable. Watch: next report (dernierCall init + first guidance archive); US consumer discretionary demand; tariff-regime changes.

== CATALYSTS ==
Next quarterly report (initializes the guidance archive); holiday-season sell-through; new-category launches; international direct-sales margin proof.

epsReported.note: GAAP diluted EPS $0.92 on GAAP net income ~$129.8M (stockanalysis.com quarterly, quarter ended 2026-06-30); adjusted net income $178M / $1.26 per diluted share excludes SBC and other items - the $0.34 wedge is the fiche's documented GAAP/adjusted gap.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No formal quarterly guide (annual guider). Q3 26 will book the $247.1M CBP tariff refund as a reduction of cost of sales (with corresponding receivable); ~half relates to 2025 duties (excluded from adjusted metrics), ~half to H1-26 (included). POS-vs-shipments gap normalizes post-Prime Day; retailer inventories healthy with room to build into Q4; management targets double-digit domestic growth in H2 with Canada returning to growth; 41st subcategory launches late Q3.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY26 RAISED HARD: net sales +16-17% (from +11.5-12.5%); adjusted EPS $6.45-6.55 (from $6.00-6.10) - of the $0.45 raise only ~$0.15 is the net tariff-refund benefit, the rest operational; adjusted EBITDA $1.36-1.37B, +19.5-20.5% (from $1.29-1.30B; ~$30M of the $67-69M raise from the refund); GAAP ETR ~22-23%; capex $190-210M tracking the high end; net interest expense down YoY. Assumes current tariffs persist (min 10% Indonesia/Malaysia/Cambodia; China/Vietnam/Thailand raised 10%->12.5%); part of the refund deliberately reinvested in retail activation, media, tech/AI and tariff mitigation.
pointsCles: Blowout Q2: net sales $1.77B +22.2% YoY (13th straight double-digit quarter, fastest pace since Q4-24), beating consensus by ~$113M; all four categories grew - Cooking & Beverage +36.5% ($499M, Luxe Cafe/Crispi), Beauty & Home Environment +65.3% ($286M), Food Prep +13.3% ($459M, BlendBOSS), Cleaning +4.1% ($522M); adjusted EPS $1.26 (+30%, $0.13 beat) vs GAAP diluted EPS $0.92 (GAAP G&A +40.8% on higher SBC).

Geographic breadth: domestic +15.5% to $1.14B (US shipments +18%, POS even higher on Prime Day timing; Canada -17% in transition, guided back to growth in H2), international +36.6% to $624M (UK +18.7% to $255M, strong France/Germany, Italy/Spain flipped to direct, LatAm/Mexico robust); distributor-to-direct conversions and the Salesforce DTC replatforming are now COMPLETE - 14 European countries live by Q4, TikTok Shop in 7 countries going to 14+ by holiday.

$247.1M tariff refund claims accepted by US CBP (July 26), to be booked in Q3 as a COGS reduction, split ~evenly between 2025 duties (excluded from adjusted metrics) and H1-26 (included); adjusted gross margin 48.7% (-70bp) still beat internal expectations on cost optimization and mix; adjusted opex leveraged for the 5th straight quarter (35.6% of sales, -40bp); cash ~$780M (+300% YoY), inventories +8.6% (healthy), H1 CFO ~$275M, ~$100M buybacks in Q2.

Core-plus-expansion narrative reinforced: management sizes TAM at ~$120B moving to $125-130B by year-end (Ninja Crispi Microwave = 40th subcategory entering a >$3B market, 41st multibillion subcategory late Q3, ~20 of 25 annual launches into existing categories); 'Jailbreak' AI agenda (Palantir promotions Phase 2, AWS media optimization live end-September, social-content capture rate lifted to 60%+) targeted at roughly flat headcount into 2027 - the next opex-leverage lever.

ancrages.moteur: Guidance FY2026 relevee au T1'26 : CA +11,5% a +12,5%, midpoint 12,0% retenu
Gradual deceleration 10%->6%, consistent with post-hypergrowth maturation and consensus revenue growth of ~9,6%/yr over 3 years (Simply Wall St)
GAAP EBIT margin expansion of +40 to +50bp/yr, consistent with the operating leverage guided on Adjusted EBITDA (+32bp in 2026), moderated by tariff pressures
GAAP tax rate maintained at 22,5% (midpoint of the 22%-23% guidance), consistent with fiscal years 2024-2025
omniumNet adds back SBC and acquisition intangibles amortisation, which management's Adjusted EPS excludes (gap of ~0,50-0,55$/share vs the non-GAAP consensus)
750M$ share buyback programme authorised Feb. 2026, started in Q1'26 (already +117M$ of net debt over the quarter); reverses the 2023-2025 deleveraging trend

Adjustment for the transaction costs tied to the JS Global separation (2023: 82,3M$ pretax), for the withholding tax on the special dividend (2023: 19,5M$) and for the exceptional discretionary bonus (2022: 34,0M$ pretax); tax normalised at 22% on the pretax add-backs

2025.residualNote: Reconciles cleanly at the company's own 22% normalized rate; net financial charge modest after the strong 2025 deleveraging (net debt 557 -> 100M).

guidanceScorecard.basisNote: Consensus is on the adjusted street basis; the Omnium base is GAAP retreated only for true separation-related one-offs (2022 bonus, 2023 separation costs) - wedge documented.

timeline.detail: Q1 26 call: FY26 adjusted EPS guide raised to $6.00-6.10 (from initial $5.90-6.00, mid 5.95, set with the FY25 release on 2026-02-11); sales guide edged up. First raise of the year on Q1 momentum (international +31.6%).

Q2 26 call: FY26 guide raised hard - net sales +16-17% (from +11.5-12.5%), adjusted EPS $6.45-6.55 (from $6.00-6.10; only ~$0.15 of the $0.45 raise from the net $247.1M CBP tariff-refund benefit), adjusted EBITDA $1.36-1.37B (+19.5-20.5%). Second raise of the year; mid now 6.50 vs initial 5.95 (+9.2%).

guidanceScorecard.paceCheckpoint: Trajectory checkpoint at creation: organic double-digit streak intact; tariff mitigation (supply-chain shift out of China) executing.

annualBeatHistory.note: Initial FY25 guidance (FY24 release, 13/02/2025): adjusted EPS 4.80-4.90$ (mid 4.85, +12/15%); realized 5.28$ - level +8.9%.

Initial FY24 guidance (FY23 release, 15/02/2024): adjusted EPS 3.45-3.61$ (mid 3.53, +7/12%); realized ~4.30$ (implied by the FY25 guide's '+12/15% vs prior' base; net sales +30%) - level +21.8%, medium precision on the realized figure.

anchorInitial.note: TRUE initial FY26 guidance (FY25 release, 11/02/2026): adjusted EPS 5.90-6.00$ (mid 5.95), net sales +10/11%. Raised at Q1 (6.00-6.10) then at Q2 to 6.45-6.55$ (incl. +0.15$ net tariff refund). REPLACES the July consensus anchor (6.12) - SharkNinja does guide annually, contrary to the fiche's initial assumption.

guidanceScorecard.applicationNote: annualBeatPct +12.3% BLENDED (in-progress +9.2 x1/2; FY25 +8.9 and FY24 +21.8 equal-shared). A serial low-baller on management's adjusted (street) basis - the Omnium base is retreated GAAP (5.51 for 2026), so apply the pattern directionally, not mechanically.

inProgress.note: Initial mid 5.95$; raised twice to 6.45-6.55$ (mid 6.50, of which ~0.15$ tariff refund) - projected +9.2%; sales guide lifted to +16/17%.
